newsitem.title: INDIA: No decision on oil price meeting - United Front.
newsitem.headline: No decision on oil price meeting - United Front.

text.p: The decision-making panel of India's ruling United Front has not yet agreed on whether to meet on June 15 to take a decision on oil prices, a United Front spokesman said on Friday.
"There is no decision yet on holding the meeting on Sunday," spokesman Jaipal Reddy told Reuters. "I cannot say it will be held."
"It has not been confirmed yet," said D. Raja, a senior leader of the Communist Party of India (CPI) and a member of the decision-making Steering Committee.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have been pressing for increases in petroleum product prices, while leftwing parties in the coalition want alternatives to be considered. A decision has been deferred several times already and a meeting was earlier scheduled for Sunday.

Domestic oil firms were owed 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March from the oil pool account deficit, which represents money owed by the government to the companies for selling below market prices.

The oil subsidy bill is estimated at some 180 billion rupees -- which includes the cost of products sold below market prices plus a cross-subsidisation element under which some products, like gasoline, are priced above market prices.
